title: clove plugin list/search envelope
description: A `clove plugin list [--all]` or `clove plugin search <text>` response. One row per plugin. Rows come from two sources that share this shape: a plugin installed on this machine (`installed: true`, with a real `path` and a probed `version`) and one discovered on crates.io but not installed (`installed: false`, `path`/`version` null, `latest_version` set). `status` is always the host<->plugin *compatibility* verdict, never registry freshness — an uninstalled row has no compatibility verdict yet and reports `available`. Discovery is strictly additive: when crates.io cannot be reached the installed rows still print, `ok` stays true, and the cause appears in `_meta.warnings`.

name.description: The bare plugin name — the binary with its `clove-` prefix removed. Derived from a *dispatchable* binary, so it always names something the resolver could actually find.

binary.description: The executable clove would dispatch to. Null only when a discovered crate ships no `clove-`-prefixed binary at all.

path.description: Absolute path of the installed executable; null for a discovered-but-not-installed plugin.

version.description: The version the installed binary reports when probed. Null when the plugin is not installed, or when the probe failed (`status: "no_info"`).

latest_version.description: The newest STABLE version published to crates.io. This — not `status` — is where "a newer release exists" lives. On a discovered row it is simply the published version. On an *installed* row it is present only when that version is strictly greater than the installed one, by the same rule `plugin update` applies, so the two can never disagree about whether an update exists.

about.description: One-line description: the plugin's own `--help` summary when installed, the crates.io description when discovered.

provides.description: Multiplexer providers the plugin claims (e.g. `github` for `clove sync github`). Empty for a discovered plugin — only a probe of the installed binary can answer this.

commands.description: The `clove ...` invocations that resolve to this plugin.

status.description: Host<->plugin compatibility verdict (PLUGIN_REGISTRY §4). `available` means "not installed here, so not yet judged".

crate.description: The crates.io crate name. Present on discovered rows; it can differ from `binary` (a crate may publish a binary under another name).

yanked.description: Every published version of the crate is yanked.

pluginListMeta.title: plugin list `_meta`
pluginListMeta.description: Row counts split by where each row came from, plus the non-fatal warnings channel. `installed_count + available_count == count` always — on `search` the counts are computed from the rows' own `installed` flags, so they cannot contradict them. `additionalProperties` is false so a new key has to be described here rather than shipping invisible to a generated client.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems — notably a discovery failure, which degrades the response rather than failing it. This is the repo-wide warnings channel, not a plugin-specific invention.
